title: Any keyword alphabet (keyword of 1-25 different letters, then A-Z), solved exactly from the clue equations with no dictionary: Quagmire III/I/II, repeating key 1-26 and sliding key period 1-26
k4_result: 520 systems (5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort form x repeating or sliding key x 26 lengths), 12,126 (system, keyword length) levels decided, 494M search steps. 458 systems have no keyword alphabet at all for keywords of 1-9 letters; 334 have none for ANY alphabet (decided to m=25). 61 systems have solutions with a keyword of 9 letters or fewer, all at long keys (repeating 16, 23, 24, 26; sliding 16-18, 23-26): in 20 of them every solution was read, in 41 only up to a shorter keyword (3-8 letters) because there are more than 50,000. 1 system (Quagmire III Beaufort, sliding 16) was decided only to 8 letters (0 solutions). In all, 1,529,661 solutions were decrypted; 0 read as English: best -5.68 over 22 quadgrams outside the clues, -6.59 with 40+ quadgrams, -6.75 with 60+ (English needs -5.1; planted answers read -4.26 to -4.92). Quagmire III, Beaufort form, repeating key: 0 alphabets of any kind at lengths 1-17, 19-22, 24, 25 (13 was open in the community's arbitrary-alphabet search); 18: none up to 16 keyword letters; 23: first solutions at 8 letters (3), 59 at 9, all 33,443 up to 11 letters read, best -6.59; 26: 13,720 up to 5 letters read, best -7.08. Vigenere form: 0 at all 26 lengths.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s, same 520 systems and same step budget: 434, 460 and 437 systems closed for keywords of 1-9 letters (K4 458); 286, 329, 305 closed for every alphabet (K4 334); 1.91M, 1.41M and 1.90M solutions read, 0 English; best readings -5.76, -5.82, -5.73 over 22 quadgrams (K4 -5.68), -6.44, -6.89, -6.67 with 40+ quadgrams (K4 -6.59), -7.02, -6.97, -6.89 with 60+ (K4 -6.75). Same picture as K4.
planted: 12/12 (keywords SANBORN, SCHEIDT and the random string ZYARKX at key lengths 13, 19 and 23 on Quagmire III Beaufort; PALIMPCEST with a sliding key of period 7; SCHEIDT on M/KR at 19; WELTZEITUHR on AZ/M at 13). Each true alphabet was listed and its reading ranked first of up to 29,654 solutions, English -4.26 to -4.92.
scope_limits: One unknown keyword alphabet of the plain kind (keyword letters, then the rest in A-Z order), used on both sides or against A-Z or KRYPTOS. NOT covered: two different unknown keywords (Quagmire IV), transposition-mixed alphabets, any key rule other than a repeating key (1-26) or a sliding key (running sum of a repeating word, period 1-26), gap slack. Budget: 6M search steps per system; 433 of 520 systems reached m=25 (every alphabet), the rest stopped between m=8 and m=22 (the Quagmire III sliding-key systems stopped at 8-16, except periods 3, 9 and 26 and, in the Beaufort form, 19). Where solutions exist the decision rests on reading them: only lists of up to 50,000 were read, so these are NOT decided beyond the stated keyword length: repeating key 26 (read to 3-5 letters), repeating 24 on M/KR (to 8), sliding 24 (to 7-8), sliding 25 (to 5-7), sliding 26 (to 3), Quagmire III sliding 16 and 18 (to 8). 523,768 of the solutions read force fewer than 20 quadgrams outside the clues and cannot be judged by English (mostly sliding keys with long periods).

negative.family: Keyword tableau with a non-dictionary keyword
negative.hypothesis: K4 is a Quagmire I, II or III cipher with a repeating or sliding key on a keyword alphabet whose keyword is not in any dictionary (a name, a German word, a misspelling, a short phrase).
negative.scope: Unknown alphabet = keyword of m different letters in any order followed by the other letters in A-Z order, m = 1..25 as far as 6M search steps per system allow (at least 8, usually 25); layouts M/M, M/AZ, M/KR, AZ/M, KR/M; Vigenere and Beaufort forms; repeating key length 1-26 and sliding key period 1-26; exact solution of the clue equations, every solution up to 50,000 per system decrypted and scored on the big English model.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: for keywords of 1-9 letters 458 of 520 systems have no solution at all (shuffled K4s: 434, 460, 437) and 334 have none for any alphabet; the 1,529,661 solutions that exist at long keys decrypt to noise, best -5.68 over 22 quadgrams and -6.59 over 40+ against -5.1 needed (shuffled best -5.73 and -6.44; planted 12/12 at -4.26 to -4.92). Not decided: repeating key 26 and sliding keys 24-26 beyond keywords of 3-8 letters, where too many alphabets pass to read.

follow_ups: Key lengths 24-26 leave 1 to 5 equations, so millions of keyword alphabets pass, but each one forces most of the plaintext (23 of 26 key letters at length 26). Do not list them: hill-climb over the keyword letters with the big English model as the score, keeping the clue equations as hard constraints (kryptos/idea86_tail.solve gives the feasible set to walk in). Planted test: a 7-letter non-word keyword at key length 26.

Quagmire IV with two unknown non-dictionary keywords: the same tail trick with two alphabets (each letter has a position on the plain side and one on the cipher side, at most 2m+1 choices each). The equations keep four letters, so the search is the same shape; count first how many (length, m1, m2) have fewer expected chance solutions than 1.

Quagmire III, Beaufort form, repeating key 18 is the last length where the community's arbitrary-alphabet search and this one both stop short (here: no keyword up to 16 letters, budget ran out). The step count roughly doubles per extra keyword letter, so about 500 times the budget (or a C port of the 60-line search) would close it for every alphabet. Length 13, also listed as unresolved there, came out closed for every alphabet in this run.

Transposition-mixed keyword alphabets without a dictionary: with keyword length w the position of a tail letter is fixed by its rank and w (column, row), so the unknowns are again 'which letters and where'. Same solver with a different position formula.
